title: tests: 58% of suite time is 7 doc walkthroughs, no way to skip
description:
Measured on snapshot 4237c43, excluding tests/trqp: 1024 passed, 14 skipped in 443 s. Seven module-scoped setup fixtures take 259 s (58%): tests/patatt/test_patch_docs.py::test_every_page_block_ran[regulars/captains/anchors] 53.6/51.6/43.8 s, tests/migrate/test_guide_captains.py 36.9 s, tests/test_guide_anchors.py 35.4 s, tests/migrate/test_guide_regulars.py 33.6 s, tests/migrate/test_rehearsal.py 6.7 s. These are not duplicates: patch_docs runs the '<!-- patch as -->' blocks that the guide tests skip. Every other test is under 3.3 s; the ~1,000 unit and integration tests together take about 185 s.

What goes wrong if it stays: every edit to git-vouch pays 7+ minutes for a full run, and a contributor who touches one parser has no documented fast loop, so they either skip tests or wait. There is no pytest.ini/pyproject marker config.

Fix (constraint, not mechanism): mark those seven modules with pytestmark = pytest.mark.slow, register the marker in one pytest.ini, and document 'pytest -m "not slow"' as the edit loop and the full run as the pre-push gate in CONTRIBUTING.md. Making the walkthroughs themselves faster depends on vouch-xlha.2/.3, since each doc block runs git vouch check against a fresh registry.
notes: Done (uncommitted): tests/conftest.py registers 'slow' and marks the 5 walkthrough modules (SLOW tuple; configure refuses a missing entry). -m 'not slow': 1251 passed in ~39 s vs ~150 s full. Doc command for CLAUDE.md pending in docs unit.
close_reason: slow marker registered in tests/conftest.py (SLOW, refuses missing modules); -m 'not slow' runs 1251 tests in ~40 s; command in doc_changes for CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md
